correctness.rationale: The published similarity characterization and homogeneity give \(\rho_{\mathcal E}(X)=\inf_S\|S^{-1}XS\|\). For an upper-triangular representative, diagonal rescaling suppresses all strict upper entries, and Ruan's direct-sum axiom gives the upper bound. For every diagonal tuple \(\lambda^{(k)}\), a norm-one functional \(\varphi_k\) with \(|\varphi_k(\lambda^{(k)})|=\|\lambda^{(k)}\|_V\) amplifies contractively; the scalar matrix \(\varphi_k(S^{-1}XS)\) is similar to an upper-triangular matrix having this value as an eigenvalue, forcing the lower bound for every similarity. Lie's theorem supplies simultaneous triangularization for solvable complex matrix Lie algebras. No numerical or finite-search evidence is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result sharpens the focal commuting-versus-general boundary in an algebraically natural direction: all simultaneously triangularizable, hence all solvable-Lie, matrix tuples are quantization-independent. It isolates non-solvability as a necessary mechanism behind the source's quantization-separation phenomenon, while covering genuinely noncommuting tuples. This structural boundary is more informative than a parameter specialization or routine example.
